problem_statement: developer-portal/website is the Jekyll-generated static site for the Fedora Developer Portal: a documentation landing site with a blue splash masthead, a logo wordmark, a top navigation bar (Start a project, Get tools, Languages & databases, Deploy and distribute), a four-panel front-nav grid, a 'Fedora Planet' blog-headlines block, a 'Share your knowledge' contribute banner, and a rich four-column footer (About, Download, Support, Join). Section pages such as /tech.html (Languages & databases) and /start.html (Start a project) reuse the same masthead/nav/footer chrome. Each docs page carries an 'On this page' section quick-nav rail (the .docs-onpage component): a labelled row of pill-shaped chips, one per section of the page, with the first chip active and a 'Reading: <Section>' readout beneath it. Clicking a chip is meant to move the active highlight to that chip and update the readout to name the selected section. Three regressions have crept into the rail and must be repaired together while keeping the rest of the Jekyll theme untouched: (1) MOBILE OVERFLOW — the chip row is pinned to a fixed non-wrapping width with fixed-width chips, so on a 390px phone it is far wider than the viewport and drags the whole homepage into horizontal scrolling; the row must wrap or reflow to fit the screen. (2) CROSS-PAGE PRESENCE — the rail currently renders only on the homepage; it must appear on every docs page (home, /tech.html, /start.html) so the section quick-nav is consistent site-wide. (3) BROKEN ACTIVE-CHIP STYLING and STALE READOUT — a bad restyle makes the active chip a near-invisible pale ghost with an illegible washed-out label and drags the chip row up over the 'On this page' eyebrow, and a wiring bug freezes the readout so clicking a chip moves the highlight but the readout text never changes from the first section. Restore a legible, high-contrast active chip in the portal's blue design language, keep the eyebrow visible, and make the readout update live to 'Reading: <Section>' for the chip the reader clicks.
required_content: The 'On this page' section quick-nav rail (.docs-onpage) renders on every docs page — the homepage, /tech.html, and /start.html — with its 'On this page' eyebrow, its per-section chips, and a 'Reading: <Section>' readout.
On a 390px mobile viewport the homepage has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance: the chip row wraps or reflows to fit the screen instead of forcing the document wider than the viewport.
The active chip is legible and high-contrast in the portal's blue design language, the 'On this page' eyebrow stays visible above the chips, and no chip overlaps the eyebrow.
Clicking a section chip updates the readout live to 'Reading: <Section>' for the clicked chip and moves the active highlight to it; the readout must not stay frozen on the first section.
The logo wordmark, top navigation, front-nav panel grid, Fedora Planet headlines, contribute banner, section pages, and the four-column footer remain present and unchanged in content and structure.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced; the site continues to serve as a self-contained static Jekyll build with locally vendored assets and no remote analytics.
design_constraints: Preserve the Fedora Developer Portal design language: blue splash masthead, Open Sans typography, Bootstrap grid rhythm, the existing nav/footer chrome, and the current section order.
Fix the section quick-nav rail (.docs-onpage) only; do not rewrite page copy, restructure sections, add or remove images, or change the top navigation.

The repair must live in the rail's own SCSS partial (_sass/_onpage.scss), its include (_includes/docs-onpage.html), and its script (static/js/onpage-nav.js); it must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html level or clipping content off-screen.
The rail and its chips must fit 390px mobile, 834px tablet, and 1440px desktop viewports; every chip and its label must remain readable at every size.
Keep the Jekyll build pipeline intact — `jekyll build` must still emit a working static _site/ served over plain HTTP.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the homepage at 1440px with the 'On this page' rail scrolled into view: the eyebrow, the row of section chips (first chip active in solid blue), and the 'Reading: Overview' readout all lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.

mobile_home captures the same homepage at 390px with the rail in view: with the defect the fixed-width chip row forces the document hundreds of pixels wider than the viewport; the repair brings horizontal overflow within tolerance by wrapping the chips.
tablet_home captures the homepage at 834px, where the rail already fits and must continue to fit.
desktop_tech and desktop_start capture /tech.html and /start.html at 1440px: the shared rail must be present on these section pages (cross-page consistency) and the nav/footer must be unchanged.
mobile_tech captures /tech.html at 390px, verifying the section page has no horizontal overflow.
desktop_home_gettools captures the homepage after clicking the 'Get tools' section chip: the highlight moves to that chip and the readout updates to 'Reading: Get tools'.

change_completion: The mobile homepage no longer overflows horizontally: the section chip row wraps to fit a 390px viewport.
Clicking a section chip updates the readout to 'Reading: <Section>' for that chip and moves the active highlight.
The active chip is rendered legibly and the 'On this page' eyebrow stays visible above the chips.
design_consistency: The rail preserves the Fedora Developer Portal identity, section order, and all surrounding content.
The section quick-nav rail is present on every docs page (home, tech, start), not just the homepage.
responsive: At 390px the chip row wraps or flexes down so the document width stays within the viewport.
At 834px and 1440px the rail lays out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Masthead, top nav, front-nav grid, Fedora Planet headlines, contribute banner, section pages, and footer remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded repair/content_asset_continuity/component task on the static Jekyll Fedora Developer Portal (jekyll build -> _site/, served over plain HTTP). The native docs lever is the site's own 'On this page' section quick-nav rail (the .docs-onpage component), a TOC-style row of section chips plus a 'Reading: <Section>' readout that is rendered as shared chrome on the home, /tech.html and /start.html docs pages. The reference rail wraps its chips (flex-wrap) so it fits 390px with zero horizontal overflow, renders on all three pages, shows a solid-blue legible active chip in the portal wordmark blue, keeps the eyebrow visible, and updates the readout live on click. The baseline leg carries the original layout defect (a fixed non-wrapping chip track that overflows mobile) and drops the rail from the section pages, but its click wiring is correct so it still updates the readout. The bad leg is a smart-wrong repair: it keeps the mobile overflow, renders a broken near-invisible washed-out active chip that collides with the eyebrow, and freezes the readout in a stale closure so clicking a chip moves the highlight but never re-labels the readout. Four orthogonal gates discriminate: no_horizontal_overflow (tolerance 24px) on mobile, visual_regression on the rail crop at desktop and mobile, cross-page dom_assertions for rail presence, and interaction_assertions for the live readout. The Fedora Developer Portal wordmark and Fedora Planet blog-headlines chrome are preserved across all legs; only the rail's SCSS partial, include, and script differ.
